chunks: And with the first chain, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'What is the status of one who denies an Imam from among you?' He said: 'He who denies an Imam from Allah and is exempt from him and his religion is an unbeliever and apostate from Islam, because the Imam is from Allah and his religion is the religion of Allah; and whoever is exempt from the religion of Allah, his blood is permissible to be killed in that state, unless he returns or repents to Allah Almighty from what he said.'

key_terms.دَمُهُ مَبَاحٌ: His blood is permissible (to be killed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who denies the Imam of their time in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the doctrine of *al-Imamah min Allah*, establishing that the Imam’s authority is divine rather than merely political, thereby making denial of the Imam equivalent to denial of Allah’s religion. It articulates the ruling of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (loyalty and disavowal), where apostasy (*murtadd*) triggers the permissibility of execution (*damuhu mubah*) unless the individual repents, reflecting the high stakes of theological fidelity in Shia jurisprudence.
